date.note: Phys. Rev. Lett. 44, 1108. Berkelman writes that CLEO and CUSB submitted their papers back to back to Physical Review Letters on 15 February 1980.

key_value_text.quote: Three narrow resonances have been observed in ... annihilation into hadrons at total energies between 9.4 and 10.4 GeV.
key_value_text.value: Three narrow resonances in e⁺e⁻ → hadrons at total energies between 9.4 and 10.4 GeV

name: Observation of Three Upsilon States
notes: The Υ was first seen at Fermilab in 1977 in hadron collisions; CESR resolved the three bound states in e+e- collisions (Berkelman).

summary.plain: In 1980 the CLEO experiment at Cornell's new CESR ring observed three narrow resonances in electron-positron collisions at total energies between 9.4 and 10.4 GeV. They were interpreted as the lowest Upsilon states of a bottom quark and its antiquark. The CUSB experiment reported the same states in a paper submitted back to back.
summary.technical: CLEO: three narrow resonances observed in e⁺e⁻ annihilation into hadrons at total energies between 9.4 and 10.4 GeV; the mass spacing and ratios of lepton-pair widths support interpreting the Υ states as the lowest triplet-S levels of the b b̄ system (Phys. Rev. Lett. 44, 1108, 1980); the first CLEO paper had 73 authors from 8 institutions.

title: Observation of Three Upsilon States
why_it_matters: Berkelman describes CESR's energy as ideal for the physics of the b quark, a gift that guaranteed the productivity of CESR; the three Υ states were the subject of the first CLEO paper, submitted in February 1980.
